To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Dangling DNS records (Dares) are a real and prevalent threat, (2) Dares can be exploited to hijack (sub)domains, (3) the underlying cause is the lack of authentication, and (4) our proposed defenses can mitigate Dares with low cost.

(i) Dares pose a significant security threat that can be easily abused by adversaries for domain and domain signing key hijacking; (ii) we have identified three attack vectors that can be used to exploit Dares; (iii) we found 467 exploitable dangling DNS records in 277 Alexa 1000 domains and 52.edu zones; (iv) we have developed three defense mechanisms that are effective in eliminating Dares and are easy for administrators to use.
